cli_result_text:
Submitted the five files needed to trace this issue:

1. **`werkzeug/local.py`** — defines `Local`, `LocalStack`, and `LocalProxy`, all backed by `contextvars.ContextVar` since Werkzeug 2.0 (per the class docstrings: "Uses `ContextVar` instead of a custom storage implementation"). `LocalProxy._get_current_object()` is the function that resolves the proxy to the real object via `ContextVar.get()`, raising `RuntimeError` (the "Working outside of..." message) via the `unbound_message` path when the var has no value in the current `Context`.

2. **`flask/globals.py`** — where Flask builds the public `request`, `session`, `g`, `current_app` proxies as `LocalProxy(_cv_request, ...)` / `LocalProxy(_cv_app, ...)`, bound to module-level `ContextVar`s `_cv_request` / `_cv_app`. This is Flask's side of the boundary described in the ticket.

3. **`flask/ctx.py`** — `RequestContext.push()`/`pop()` and `AppContext.push()`/`pop()`, which call `_cv_request.set(self)` / `_cv_app.reset(token)`. This is where the context value actually gets bound into the *current* `contextvars.Context` — critically, `ContextVar.set()` only affects the Context object active in the calling task/thread, which is the root of the customer's bug.

4. **`flask/app.py`** — contains `ensure_sync`/async view wrapping (async views run via `asgiref.async_to_sync` inside the request-bound context), showing why the *view itself* has request context but anything it spawns off to a separate asyncio Task afterward runs in a fresh copy.

5. **`docs/async-await.rst`** — Flask's own documented explanation ("Background tasks" section) that `asyncio.create_task` inside an async view will have its task cancelled when the view's event loop stops, and that spawned tasks aren't a supported background-task mechanism under Flask's WSGI-based async model — directly explaining the customer's observed `RuntimeError`.
